title: The Year of the Four Emperors (AD 69)
lead: In AD 69 the Roman Empire had four emperors: Galba, Otho, Vitellius and Vespasian. Tacitus opens his Histories with this year, and Josephus tells the same civil wars in a few lines while his own war in Judea waited.

sections.b:
Nero died on 9 June 68. Galba, already acclaimed in Spain, was recognized in Rome. On 10 January 69 he adopted Piso as his heir (Tacitus gives the day as the fourth day before the Ides, 1:18). On the eighteenth day before the Kalends of February, which is 15 January, Otho's coup killed Galba and Piso (1:27; the Wikipedia page on the year also gives 15 January). On 1 January the 4th and 22nd legions tore down Galba's images (1:55), and on 3 January the army of Upper Germany declared for Vitellius (1:57). Otho lost at Bedriacum on 14 April and took his own life soon after: Wikipedia's page on the year says the next day, its page on Otho gives his reign as ending 16 April, Josephus counts his reign as three months and two days (Jewish War 4.9.9) and Suetonius the ninety-fifth day (Otho 11). The Senate recognized Vitellius on 19 April. Tiberius Alexander made the legions at Alexandria swear to Vespasian on 1 July, the army of Judea swore on 3 July (Tacitus 2:79), and before 15 July all Syria had taken the same oath (2:81). Antonius Primus and the Danube legions won the second battle at Bedriacum on 24 October. Vitellius was killed on 20 December and the Senate recognized Vespasian on 21 December. The dates for Nero's death, the first Bedriacum, the Senate's recognition of Vitellius, the second Bedriacum and the last two days are those of Wikipedia's page on the year. The days given with a Tacitus reference are his own.

Josephus gives the lengths of two reigns: Galba reigned seven months and seven days, and Otho three months and two days (Jewish War 4.9.2 and 4.9.9, in Whiston's chapter and section numbers). Tacitus's Book 1 runs from 1 January to Otho's departure from Rome on 14 March.

sections.b: The Jewish revolt of AD 66 to 70 was in the middle of this year. Josephus says Vespasian put off his attack on Jerusalem and waited to see where the empire would go after Nero (Jewish War 4.9.2), and that Titus was sailing to greet Galba when he heard Galba was dead. Jesus had told his disciples, "You are going to hear of wars and reports of wars. Take care not to panic. This has to happen, but the end is not here yet" (Matthew 24:6), and had spoken of Jerusalem "being encircled by army camps" (Luke 21:20). Those verses do not say the civil wars of 69 are in view; the link is background. Some readers of Revelation count the short reigns of 69 among the "seven kings" (Revelation 17:10); the site's note on that verse sets out the counts.
